definitions.explanation: A person who takes on the role of listening in a conversation, or the act of serving as the listener rather than the speaker.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{聞|き}き{役|やく}に{徹|てっ}した。
examples.english: Today I devoted myself to being the listener.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はいつも{聞|き}き{役|やく}に{回|まわ}るタイプだ。
examples.english: He's the type who always ends up being the listener.

examples.japanese: いい{聞|き}き{役|やく}になることが、{信頼|しんらい}{関係|かんけい}を{築|きず}く{第一歩|だいいっぽ}だ。
examples.english: Being a good listener is the first step in building a relationship of trust.

notes:
A compound noun from {聞|き}く (to listen) + {役|やく} (role). Refers to the person who primarily listens in a conversation, or the act of taking on that role. In Japanese communication, being a good {聞|き}き{役|やく} is considered an important social skill.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {聞|き}き{役|やく}に{徹|てっ}する — to devote oneself to listening
- {聞|き}き{役|やく}に{回|まわ}る — to take on the role of listener
- いい{聞|き}き{役|やく} — a good listener
- {聞|き}き{役|やく}になる — to become the listener

RELATED WORDS:
- {話|はな}し{役|やく} — the speaker role; the counterpart to {聞|き}き{役|やく}
- {相槌|あいづち} — conversational back-channeling; a key skill for being a good {聞|き}き{役|やく}
